messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Elevated error rate (5xx) observed across Console->ControlPlane API calls in us-west-2 starting ~1918123200. Paging oncall.
oncall-ryan: I’m on it — joining bridge now. any customer-facing outages? cc @cs-bot for impact
cs-bot: Observed ~12 customer sessions with console UI errors (500) in the last 7m. No new support tickets yet; monitoring.
sanjay: quick hypothesis: config push to control-plane feature-flag service failed, consoles are getting stale config and returning 502 for some endpoints. Seeing spike in controlplane logs around 1918123160.
marta: timeline pls — can someone paste the related deploys / flag changes in the last 30m?
lina: I can pull deployment events. saw a rollout for controlplane-config-service at 1918123122 (image: config-service:v2.4.1). It had 1 rollback attempt earlier but ended successfully.
alex: adding logs from edge-router (filtered):
```
[us-west-2][1918123189] upstream=controlplane-api id=svc-ctrl-14 status=502 path=/v1/config/flags user=console-service
[us-west-2][1918123194] upstream=controlplane-api id=svc-ctrl-14 status=200 path=/v1/health
[us-west-2][1918123201] upstream=controlplane-api id=svc-ctrl-14 status=502 path=/v1/config/flags user=console-service
```
oncall-ryan: ok, so intermittent 502s to /v1/config/flags. That matches console errors. mitigation idea: switch consoles to fallback cached config while we investigate. Can we toggle fallback for the cluster?
sanjay: fallback TTL can be set via feature-flag TTL override in the controlplane. I can patch it to longer for us-west-2.
marta: who has permission to toggle? I don't want to touch production without ops approval.
oncall-ryan: I have perms. @sanjay, if you prepare the patch I’ll apply and roll back if it causes regression.
sanjay: applying patch in 2m — will post the kubectl command.
```
# extend console config cache TTL for us-west-2
kubectl -n infra patch configmap console-config --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/flags_cache_ttl","value":"900"}]' --context=prod-us-west-2
```
lina: while that's running I'm starting a tail of controlplane pods for 502 stack traces:
```
kubectl -n controlplane logs -l app=controlplane-api --since=15m --context=prod-us-west-2 | grep "502" -n -C3 | tail -50
```
alex: I'm also pulling quick correlation from telemetry (request id sample) — sending a few request-ids here for deeper trace: req-ids [r-7fa2, r-7fa3, r-7fa9]
oncall-ryan: patch applied at 1918123560. consoles should now fall back to cached config for 15m. cs-bot, can you verify customer sessions?
cs-bot: Re-checking: customer error rate dropped from 12 sessions to 2 within ~45s after patch. No new high-severity tickets. :thumbsup:
sanjay: logs show burst of HTTP 502 caused by timeout to feature-flag backend connections: stdout stack shows "Upstream request timed out after 1500ms" at 1918123188.
alex: copying a snippet from controlplane pod:
```
ERROR controllers/featureflags.go:142 upstream request timed out after 1500ms, attempted host: ff-service.prod.svc.cluster.local:8080
goroutine 2345 [running]:
  net/http.(*persistConn).writeLoop
```
marta: so root cause candidate: ff-service instances failing or overloaded after config rollout. Could be new image (v2.4.1) regressing perf or a bad connection pool setting.
lina: I've verified ff-service pod CPU spikes around 1918123150 and repeated restarts of one replica at 1918123220.
oncall-ryan: plan: 1) keep TTL fallback in place 2) scale ff-service to +2 replicas 3) gather logs for RCA and correlate with deploy 4) prepare rollback of config-service image if scaling doesn't stabilize.
sanjay: scaling now:
```
kubectl -n platform scale deployment ff-service --replicas=5 --context=prod-us-west-2
```
alex: scaling executed at 1918123625. monitoring for errors.
cs-bot: customer impact: 95% of sessions recovered, listed customers with errors: [acme-inc, edu-labs, searchly]. Opening support tickets for the 3 with ops note.
marta: for RCA thread we'll need timeline + logs + deploy diff + metrics for ff-service. I'll create an inc-rca doc but add preliminary notes here.

--- TIMELINE (working) ---
1918123122 controlplane-config-service rollout start (v2.4.1)
1918123150 ff-service CPU spike, some restarts
1918123160 first 502 observed in edge-router logs
1918123188 telemetry traces show timeouts to ff-service
1918123220 ff-service replica restart
1918123560 TTL fallback patch applied
1918123625 ff-service scaled from 3 -> 5

--- HYPOTHESES ---
- H1: config-service rollout introduced a regression in its ff-client connection pooling leading to timeouts (most likely)
- H2: ff-service itself had a transient resource pressure / kernel-level networking blip
- H3: controlplane sidecar resource limit misconfiguration causing occasional GC pauses

--- ACTION ITEMS ---
- marta: start inc-rca doc + collect deploy diff (image tags, env changes)
- alex: export full traces for req-ids and upload to S3 (link TBD)
- lina: collect core dumps / container restarts and node metrics
- sanjay: open PR to revert config-service to v2.4.0 if scaling doesn't help by +15m
- ryan: notify PagerDuty to mark incident as mitigated if errors < 0.5% for 10m

sanjay: also note: config-service had a change to connection timeout from 800ms -> 1500ms in v2.4.1, so paradoxically it waits longer and exhausts client pools. That could explain backlog.
alex: capturing a quick grep of feature-flag client logs showing "conn pool exhausted" occurrences:
```
WARN ffclient/pool.go:88 conn pool exhausted, waiting for free conn
WARN ffclient/pool.go:92 timeout waiting for conn
```
oncall-ryan: good catch. That points strongly to H1. marta — please mark H1 highest priority.
marta: noted. I'm adding a short mitigation note: rollback config-service to v2.4.0 if we see more customer errors after scaling and TTL patch expires.

--- LOG SHARING ---
alex: uploaded raw logs + traces to s3://redwood-incident-logs/1918123456/ (private link sent to incident channel). Will add access to marta, sanjay, lina.

--- HANDOFF PLAN ---
oncall-ryan: I'm handing off to sanjay for the overnight watch at 1918127000. sanjay, you're primary; if perf doesn't stabilize we do the rollback. I'll leave the bridge open for 2h then close.
sanjay: ack. I'll monitor metrics and if error rate >0.5% for 10m initiate rollback. I'll post runbook steps here when ready.

oncall-ryan: final note before bridge: customers are minimally impacted, mitigation applied (TTL fallback + scale). Keeping as Sev-2 and moving to RCA. Thanks all :heart:
marta: creating RCA doc link: https://docs.redwood.example/incidents/1918123456-rca (placeholder) — will fill in details.
cs-bot: Notifying Customer Success cohort: summary posted to #customer-impact with tag @cs-leads.
